slides.title: Eligibility is income per member, so household size decides who is counted
slides.text: The rule of the network Eligibility is income per member, so household size decides who is counted Eligible: an active household whose monthly income per member is at most 1,000 SAR Income 6,000 SAR with 5 members: 1,200 per member, not eligible The same income with 7 members: 857 per member, eligible A household with no recorded size cannot be classified at all Why this matters on Day 3 Household size is blank for 18% of the population of the question. slides.title: Files, an API and a database fail in three different ways
slides.text: How data arrive Files, an API and a database fail in three different ways Files Nothing describes them. Encoding, date layout and units are in nobody's head but the sender's. A file can come twice or not at all. An API Data come in pages, the service can be busy, and records change while you read. It usually states a total. A database Types and keys are declared, but only the ones somebody declared. Your query decides what you see. One habit covers all three: before reading a value, count what arrived against what the source says it sent.

slides.title: Load every column as text first; decide types later, in steps you can count
slides.text: Recap of FN-104, one step further Load every column as text first; decide types later, in steps you can count B01 reads as UTF-8. B03 fails at its first Arabic name: it is in Windows-1256 B08 opens, but begins with three extra bytes, EF BB BF: a byte order mark that a spreadsheet wrote A loader that guesses types reads 03/07/2026 as March or as July, and does not say which As text, nothing is lost: 14 files, 210,000 rows, every repair still ahead and countable What goes wrong. The mark becomes part of the first column name, and log_id is "not found" in one file of fourteen.

slides.title: Follow next until it is null, and expect a busy answer
slides.text: Reading an API Follow next until it is null, and expect a busy answer records, url = [], "/v1/donations?page=1&per_page=200" while url: page = G.get_json(base + url) # retries a 503 records += page["data"] total, url = page["total"], page["next"] The address of the next page comes from the answer; do not compute it 503 means "busy, ask again": wait, retry, give up after a few tries Keep the total the service reports: it is its claim about itself

slides.title: Somebody will ask where a number came from, and you will not be in the room

Were we allowed to use it for this? What is it known not to cover? A provenance record One short record per source, kept in the repository beside the code, changed in the same commit as the extract it describes.

slides.title: Six fields, and what a reviewer needs to read in each
slides.text: The record Six fields, and what a reviewer needs to read in each Field A reviewer needs origin the system, and how the extract was made owner the person to ask, by role coverage which units, which period, and who is not in it sharing basis the consent, agreement or approval, and its purpose refresh date the day your copy was taken limits what the data cannot be trusted for The labs add a seventh key, the classification level of the source.

slides.title: Holding an extract is not permission to use it for the next question
slides.text: On what basis Holding an extract is not permission to use it for the next question The register extract came under approval DS-2026-041, for service coverage analysis, Q3 2026 The approval names a purpose, the people who may see the data, and that identified records go no further A new question next year is a new request to the data protection officer In the Data Sharing Policy Among its principles: sharing serves a legitimate purpose, and access is authorised on a need-to-know and least-privilege basis.

slides.title: Three of the four sources are Restricted; one is Public
slides.text: The seventh key Three of the four sources are Restricted; one is Public Source Level Because register Restricted personal data of beneficiaries branch logs Restricted household ids and names of collectors donations API Restricted internal operations, no donor names open district table Public published under an open licence The national policy has four levels: Top Secret, Secret, Restricted and Public. Anything joined to a Restricted source is at least Restricted.

slides.title: The open table has three dates, and only one is the refresh date
slides.text: Open data has provenance too The open table has three dates, and only one is the refresh date 2022 The year the rows describe. It belongs in coverage. 15 March 2023 The day it was published. It identifies the release, in origin. 2 October 2026 The day our copy was downloaded: the refresh date. And the gap between them is a limit. A table about 2022 used in 2026 describes a city that has since grown, unevenly.

slides.title: Under-coverage is whole households missing, and not at random
slides.text: A first kind of missing data Under-coverage is whole households missing, and not at random Missing values: the household is there, a field is blank. Day 3, Sessions 1 to 3 Missing units: the household is not in the data at all Households far from a branch register less; they are also the ones served least The headline is therefore too kind to exactly the districts it is meant to find No repair, only a report No imputation of a field brings back a household that was never listed. The coverage table goes beside the headline.

"Low coverage means low need." "Coverage above 100% shows fabricated households."

slides.title: Encodings and Arabic text
slides.text: Session 1 Encodings and Arabic text Decode a file line by line and count each encoding Repair names that were decoded twice Normalise Arabic letters and digits into a key and log every repair 01

slides.title: A line of the register is in one of three states, and no encoding reads them all
slides.text: One file, appended from 14 exports A line of the register is in one of three states, and no encoding reads them all State What you see Lines UTF-8, correct ماجد محمد باوزير most Windows-1256 bytes (B03, B11) fails as UTF-8 5,458 UTF-8 that was decoded twice (B06) ط¨ظ†ط¯ط± …: valid UTF-8, wrong letters 2,732 names What goes wrong. Reading the whole file as Windows-1256 raises no error: every byte is a letter in that code page. The 34,542 UTF-8 lines become nonsense, quietly.

slides.title: Decide per line: valid UTF-8 is UTF-8; what is not is the legacy code page
slides.text: The decision rule Decide per line: valid UTF-8 is UTF-8; what is not is the legacy code page def decode(b: bytes): try: return b.decode("utf-8"), "utf-8" except UnicodeDecodeError: return b.decode("cp1256"), "cp1256" Arabic in Windows-1256 is almost never valid UTF-8, so the test is safe in this direction Return the encoding with the text and count it The count has a shape: all 5,458 lines are from two branches. A scatter over all branches would mean the rule is wrong

slides.title: Undo the wrong step, and prove the rule leaves correct text alone
slides.text: The state that raises no error anywhere Undo the wrong step, and prove the rule leaves correct text alone 1 · Typed بندر stored as UTF-8 bytes → 2 · Misread the branch system read the bytes as Windows-1256 and saved the result → 3 · Repair s.encode("cp1256").decode("utf-8") Correct Arabic does not survive that round trip: the decode fails and the function returns the text unchanged So the function is safe on all 40,000 names, and changes 2,732, every one at B06

slides.title: A key is a normalised copy for matching; the stored name is never replaced
slides.text: After the bytes, the letters A key is a normalised copy for matching; the stored name is never replaced Rule Example drop marks and the stretch mark مُحمّد → محمد one alef; ى → ي; ة → ه أحمد → احمد join عبد to the next word عبد الله → عبدالله one space between words trailing and double spaces go 24,355 distinct Arabic names as typed are 21,252 distinct keys: about one "different" name in eight was a spelling variant.

slides.title: An ID number typed in Arabic-Indic digits is a different string
slides.text: Digits are text too An ID number typed in Arabic-Indic digits is a different string 39,851 → 39,820 distinct national ids, before and after the digit rule One branch typed 2,784 ID numbers as ١٠٩٠… 31 households registered there and again elsewhere: one person, two strings A count of distinct people, or a join on the id, was wrong with no error Normalise digits in every key before you compare it with anything

slides.title: A repair that is not counted cannot be checked, repeated or reversed
slides.text: The habit of the day A repair that is not counted cannot be checked, repeated or reversed A rule Written as code, applied to every row, never by hand to a few. A count One line per rule in a log: how many rows it changed, and where. The original Kept beside the repaired value, so a reviewer can disagree. The same three in every lab today: a repair log, a join log, a threshold table, a change log.

slides.text: Session 2 Keys and cardinality Repair mistyped keys by stated rules Test many-to-one before joining Reconcile rows in with rows out plus rows set aside 02

slides.title: A join can lose rows, add rows, and report neither
slides.text: Many handouts, one household A join can lose rows, add rows, and report neither Lost A key typed by hand does not match. In an inner join the handout disappears. Added A household that is in the register twice gets every handout twice. Unnoticed The result is a table of plausible size. Nothing compares it with what went in. The remedy has three parts, in this order: repair keys by rule, test the cardinality, count rows at every step.

slides.title: A repair is safe when it cannot change which household is meant
slides.text: Lab 2.2, step 1 A repair is safe when it cannot change which household is meant As typed Rule Safe because h482913 upper-case case carries no information in this id H482913 strip spaces nor do spaces H-482913 remove the hyphen nor a separator H48O913 letter O to digit 0 after the H only digits are possible Never a repair: replacing an id by "the most similar one in the register". That picks a household, and it can pick the wrong one.

slides.title: Matching without a clean key
slides.text: Session 3 Matching without a clean key Block and score candidate pairs Measure false matches and missed matches on labelled pairs Choose a threshold and state its cost 03

slides.title: 300 handouts were written on paper, with a name and no id
slides.text: The problem 300 handouts were written on paper, with a name and no id A satellite point of B04 and B05, during Ramadan A name, a district ticked on the form, a phone for seven in ten 4,937 active households of the two branches to search Staff labelled 848 candidate pairs by hand: 255 true, 593 not Two errors, two prices Missed match: a handout stays uncounted, and you can see it. False match: one family is credited with another's parcels, and it looks like a success.

slides.title: Block, score, decide
slides.text: Three steps Block, score, decide 1 · Block compare only pairs that agree on a reliable field: the district → 2 · Score how alike are the two name keys, from 0 to 100 → 3 · Decide accept, reject, or send to a person Blocking: 311,703 candidate pairs instead of 1,481,100, and all 255 true pairs survive it A true pair that disagrees on the blocking field is never compared: check that on the labelled pairs

slides.title: A higher threshold buys fewer false matches with more missed ones
slides.text: Measured on the 848 labelled pairs A higher threshold buys fewer false matches with more missed ones Rule Accepted False False-match rate Missed of 255 name score ≥ 70 309 86 27.8% 32 name score ≥ 85 149 11 7.4% 117 name score ≥ 95 117 4 3.4% 142 No threshold gives both. Even at 95, four accepted pairs are the wrong family, and more than half of the true pairs are missed.

slides.title: A second field breaks the trade
slides.text: Lab 2.3, step 4 A second field breaks the trade 172 · 0 pairs accepted and false matches, when names are alike and phones agree on nine of ten digits Two fields that agree by accident are rare; one field that agrees by accident is common 83 true pairs are not accepted: mostly walk-ins who gave no phone They go to a review queue for a person, not through a lower threshold

slides.title: Accept, reject, or ask a person
slides.text: The decision has three outcomes Accept, reject, or ask a person Accept automatically The rule that showed no false match on labelled pairs. 172 of 300 walk-ins. Review Likely names without a phone, or several candidates. A person decides, and the decision is recorded. Leave unmatched 45 walk-ins are new households. An unmatched record is an honest result. Report it like a join: 300 records in, so many matched by rule, so many by review, so many unmatched.

slides.title: Which rule goes into the build?

slides.title: A blank can depend on nothing, on what you see, or on the value itself
slides.text: Three mechanisms A blank can depend on nothing, on what you see, or on the value itself Mechanism The blank depends on Dropping the rows MCAR · completely at random nothing loses precision, adds no bias MAR · at random given what is recorded fields you can see: a branch, a date biased, unless you work within those fields MNAR · not at random the missing value itself biased, and the recorded data cannot show by how much The names are Rubin's (1976). They describe the relation between a blank and the data, not a property of a column: one column can hold all three.

It does not tell MAR from MNAR

slides.title: "Which estimate is right?" cannot be answered. "How far can it move?" can

"How far can it move?" can 1 · Logical bounds assume nothing about the blank households → 2 · A plausible range assumptions you can defend, stated → 3 · A recommendation one estimate, its range, its reason A sensitivity analysis varies what you assumed and reports what happens to the conclusion. It does not make the missing data less missing.

slides.text: Lab 4.2, step 1 A new batch arrives, and seven column rules fail Rule that fails Rows validity: weight_kg between 5 and 50 278 completeness: household_key 60 uniqueness: log_id 50 validity: parcels between 1 and 3 40 validity: district_id 20 type: handout_date 15 validity: household_size 12 The first week of October: 4,180 rows, built as the quarter was Each line names what somebody can fix Look again at the first line: 278 handouts above 50 kg. Is that all that is wrong with those rows?

slides.title: B05 sent pounds. Most of its rows pass the range rule
slides.text: What a column rule cannot see B05 sent pounds. Most of its rows pass the range rule 278 · 377 rows of B05 caught by "5 to 50 kg", and rows of B05 that are wrong A parcel weighs about 12 kg: about 26 in pounds One parcel in pounds: 26, inside 5 to 50. Passes Two or three parcels in pounds: 53 or 79. Fails The value is fine on its own. It is wrong for its number of parcels

slides.title: Two rules across fields
slides.text: Lab 4.2, step 2 Two rules across fields def not_per_parcel(df): ok = df.parcels.between(1, 3) per = df.weight_kg / df.parcels.where(ok) return df[per.notna() & ~per.between(9, 15)] def before_registration(df): return df[date(df.handout_date) < date(df.registered_on)] 9 to 15 kg per parcel: all 377 rows of B05, and no row of any other branch Handout on or after registration: 30 rows in 12 branches. A household cannot collect before it exists: a wrong key or a wrong date Each rule skips rows that another rule already reports, so one fault gives one line

slides.title: A branch cannot hand out more food than it received
slides.text: Lab 4.2, step 3 A branch cannot hand out more food than it received B05 · received in the week 9,574 kg B05 · handed out, as recorded 20,005 kg The logs say what went out; the donations source says what came in. No single table holds both To compare them: the same unit, the same week, one row per branch. A small pipeline of its own It catches a whole class of faults that leave every row plausible

slides.title: A failure report says whose rows, and what to look at
slides.text: Lab 4.2, step 4 A failure report says whose rows, and what to look at Rule Rows Whose What to look at consistency: 9 to 15 kg per parcel 377 B05: 377 median 26.4 per parcel: pounds entered as kilograms? consistency: handout on or after registration 30 12 branches the household id or the date of these handouts consistency across sources: handed out no more than received 1 B05 handed 20,005 kg, received 9,574 kg Ten lines in all. Seven from the column rules, three from the rules you add. "Validation failed" helps nobody; a line that names the branch gets fixed.

slides.title: Reject the file, or set the rows aside?
slides.text: Recap of FN-104, as a rule of the build Reject the file, or set the rows aside? Reject the file The fault is in how the file was made: a wrong unit, a wrong layout, a missing column. Every row of B05 is suspect. Send it back. Quarantine the rows The fault is in single rows: a blank key, a date before registration. Load the rest; set these aside with a reason and count them in the log. Either way the decision is made per rule, in advance, and the log shows it: rows in equal rows loaded plus rows set aside.

slides.title: Which rule finds it?
slides.text: Checkpoint Which rule finds it? From 7 to 9 August a branch writes dates as month/day/year; the build reads that branch as day/month/year. Every date parses, and every one falls inside the quarter. Which rule is most likely to show the fault? Type: the date matches the pattern of the file Completeness: no date is missing Validity: the date is inside the quarter Consistency: rows per branch per day against that branch's usual pattern

slides.title: Minimise and pseudonymise
slides.text: Session 3 Minimise and pseudonymise Re-link a plain hash with a list and by enumeration Replace identifiers with a keyed hash Measure uniqueness on quasi-identifiers and reduce it by generalising 03

slides.title: The safest field is the one that never entered the dataset
slides.text: Before any technique The safest field is the one that never entered the dataset Lab 1.1 listed the fields the question needs. A name, a phone number and an ID number are not among them They were needed for one step: matching the 300 walk-in records of Day 2 After that step they are dropped, and the dataset keeps a key that says "the same household" and nothing else Minimise, then pseudonymise First ask whether the field is needed at all. Only for what remains: how to replace the identifier so that tables still join.

slides.title: Pseudonymised data is still personal data
slides.text: Recap of FN-106 Pseudonymised data is still personal data Pseudonymised Identifiers are replaced by codes. Linking back needs additional information, which is kept separately under its own controls. Somebody can still link back, so the data stays personal. Anonymised Nobody can link the data to a person any more, with any reasonable means. A much higher bar, and rarely reached by a table with one row per household. The national guideline names generalisation and aggregation among the techniques: age bands in place of ages, a year in place of a date. Lab 4.3 uses both.

slides.title: "A hash cannot be reversed." Nobody needs to reverse it
slides.text: Lab 4.3, steps 1 and 2 "A hash cannot be reversed." Nobody needs to reverse it 5,000 of 5,000 people on a known list re-identified in a table of plain SHA-256 hashes The same input gives the same hash, for everyone List attack : hash the ID numbers you hold; join Enumeration : an ID number has ten digits. Hash every possible one The 2,000,000 numbers of the course range take seconds on a laptop; all ten-digit numbers take hours

slides.title: A keyed hash: without the key, neither attack starts
slides.text: Lab 4.3, step 3 A keyed hash: without the key, neither attack starts import hmac, hashlib, os key = os.environ["GHILAL_KEY"].encode() def pseudonym(s: str) -> str: return hmac.new(key, s.encode(), hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()[:16] Stable and unique: the same household has the same pseudonym in every table, so joins still work The key is the "additional information": kept separately, never committed, never sent A list attack without the key: 0 of 5,000 A new key gives new pseudonyms: two recipients cannot join their tables to each other

slides.title: The key holds, and ordinary fields still single households out
slides.text: Lab 4.3, step 4 The key holds, and ordinary fields still single households out district, exact date, exact size 92.8% district, year, size band 0.0% Share of the 37,333 households whose combination of fields occurs exactly once. "They live in D09, registered on 14 March 2024, seven of them": a neighbour needs no key A combination of ordinary fields that singles a person out is a quasi-identifier Generalised, the smallest group has 4 households; the partner can still count shared households

slides.title: The classification of the source decides the conditions of sharing
slides.text: Who may receive what The classification of the source decides the conditions of sharing Stays inside Raw sources. Rows with identifiers as typed. The key. Under an agreement Household-level tables, pseudonymised and generalised: to named people, for one purpose, for a stated time. May be published Aggregates by district that single nobody out, the code, the rules, the report. The provenance records of Day 1 classified the register and the logs as Restricted. A table derived from them does not become Public by losing a column.

slides.title: What must change before the table is sent?
slides.text: Checkpoint What must change before the table is sent? A table for a partner holds, per household: a keyed-hash pseudonym, the district, the exact registration date and the household size. The key is stored safely. What is the remaining risk, and the remedy? The pseudonym can be enumerated; use a longer hash Date, district and size single households out; send the year and a size band None: without names and ID numbers the table is anonymous The pseudonym links tables; remove it and keep the other fields

slides.title: No number in the report is typed by hand
slides.text: Lab 4.4, step 2 No number in the report is typed by hand def headline(facts): lo, hi = facts["range"] return (f"an estimated " f"{facts['recommended']} parcels " f"per eligible household per month " f"(plausible range {lo} to {hi}; " f"standard {facts['standard']})") The next rebuild changes the numbers. A typed number stays, and the report then describes a dataset that no longer exists The lab checks it: every number in your headline must occur in the facts the build wrote An AI-assistant may improve the wording after your draft exists. The numbers still come from the build
